issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore that holds an array of Book named `books` and an initializer `init(books: [Book])`. In the solution, the Bookstore class declares a property `inventory: [Book]` but the initializer and client code use `books` (initializer assigns to `self.books` and Client accesses `bookstore.books`). This name mismatch between the declared property (`inventory`) and the expected/used property (`books`) is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confusion about the intended property name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore property name consistent with the problem statement and client code. Rename the declared property `inventory` to `books` (e.g. `let books: [Book]`) and ensure the initializer assigns to `self.books = books`. Alternatively, update all references (including the problem statement and Client) to use `inventory` consistently, but keeping `books` is recommended to match the spec.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the Bookstore to hold an array of Book objects named `books` and defines an initializer signature `init(books: [Book])`. In the provided solution the Bookstore declares the stored property as `inventory` but the initializer and client code use `books` (and the initializer assigns to a non-existent `self.books`). This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual property across problem and solution (and internally within the solution) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (`books`) to the implementation (`inventory`) and leads to an incorrect/compiling solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent property name for the Bookstore's collection across all artifacts. Rename the stored property to `books` in Bookstore (or alternatively change all usages to `inventory` and update the problem statement), and ensure the initializer assigns to the same property (e.g. `self.books = books`). Update all client code to reference the same identifier.
